title: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq under ANT after record $81 billion IPO
subtitle: The stock debuts Thursday at a $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation with gray-market and prediction-market trading pointing to a 20% to 26% opening premium over the $83 offer price.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The company priced its IPO Wednesday evening at $83 per share, above its filed $70 to $78 range, and sold roughly 980 million Class A shares for about $81.3 billion. CNBC puts the fully diluted market cap at approximately $1.5 trillion. Including the greenshoe option, the raise could rise to $93.5 billion. Nasdaq 100 futures jumped about 2.1% before the open, and Bloomberg — citing gray-market trading — reported the stock could open 20% to 26% above the offer price.

The debut sets the single largest IPO on record, topping the $75 billion SpaceX raise from June. The $83 price above the top of range is the detail that matters: underwriters pulled it off because the book closed six to seven times oversubscribed, and the private placement of non-voting shares — Google is one of seven strategic buyers — brings the combined public-plus-private raise near $90 billion. A prediction-market tracker gives 43% odds the first-day close lands between $1.25 and $1.5 trillion, which would place Anthropic among the ten most valuable public companies on day one.

This closes a pricing week that began with NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 blowout on Monday and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 launch on Tuesday. The three events form a single capital-market reading: the chip vendor delivered, the frontier lab shipped, and the safety-first lab tested whether public investors will pay what private markets have been pricing for two years. CNBC also reported that OpenAI has filed confidentially for its own IPO, with a 2027 debut likely — a filing that depends directly on how ANT trades today and over the next two weeks.

For learners: an opening-day pop of 20% or more is engineered, not accidental. Underwriters hold back allocation and price under what the book would bear so the stock prints green and institutional buyers stay happy — the cost is dilution the company absorbed by not pricing higher. Whether ANT closes at $1.3 trillion or $1.6 trillion matters less than the signal that follows: if this prints green, OpenAI files faster, and the private valuations of every other frontier lab reprice overnight.
